findings.original: If the graph needs more colours than there are registers, some variables are **spilled** to memory.
findings.correction: If the fixed graph needs more colours than there are registers, it cannot be allocated as-is. An allocator can **spill** values to memory or transform live ranges, for example by splitting or rematerializing values.
findings.reason: Insufficient colors do not force spilling when program transformations can change the interference graph.

findings.original: The **four colour theorem** says every planar map can be coloured with 4 colours.
findings.correction: The **four colour theorem** says every finite simple planar graph can be properly vertex-coloured with at most 4 colours. For maps, this corresponds to connected regions sharing a boundary segment; meeting at one point does not require different colours.
findings.reason: Specify the actual graph theorem and map-region convention.

findings.original: each independently uniform random base has a false-pass probability at most 1/4
findings.correction: For a fixed odd composite n, each independently uniform base from 1 through n − 1 has a false-pass probability at most 1/4
findings.reason: Uniform randomness requires a specified base domain.

findings.original: Diffie–Hellman key exchange relies on the same modular exponentiation, with the hardness coming from discrete logarithms instead of factoring.
findings.correction: Finite-field Diffie–Hellman uses modular exponentiation. Recovering its shared secret from public group elements is the computational Diffie–Hellman problem; solving discrete logarithms would solve it, but those hardness assumptions must not simply be equated. Authentication and the full protocol introduce additional requirements.
findings.reason: DLP hardness alone is not the same claim as CDH hardness; finite-field qualifier also excludes elliptic-curve exponentiation conflation.

findings.question: disc-number-theory-q8
findings.original: In RSA, knowing φ(n) is equivalent to knowing p and q, which is why it's kept secret.
findings.correction: For this two-prime RSA modulus, knowing n and φ(n) reveals p + q = n − φ(n) + 1. The roots of t² − (p + q)t + n are p and q, so φ(n) must remain secret.
findings.reason: State the known-modulus and distinct-two-prime assumptions and constructive recovery.

findings.question: disc-number-theory-q9
findings.original: d must invert e mod φ(n) = 40, not mod n.
findings.correction: The construction here inverts e mod φ(n) = 40; more generally, RSA permits an inverse modulo λ(n) = lcm(4, 10) = 20. The value 37 satisfies neither requirement.
findings.reason: An inverse modulo phi is sufficient but not necessary; avoid contradicting the later lambda qualification.

limitations: All six lesson bodies and 72 complete question records independently read, including distractors, explanations, worked examples and answer keys. Targeted primary-source verification and direct mathematical reasoning were used; this is not a claim of an exhaustive sentence-to-source map.

All 12 Python lesson fences and eight quiz fences executed by an independently inspected and rerun author harness; 18,663 assertions pass. This includes all 1,099 labelled simple graphs through five vertices for bipartite checks, exhaustive small relation/function counts, GCD/extended-GCD/sieve/modular-power cases, all toy RSA message representatives, and SQLite three-valued De Morgan checks.

Additional verifier harness passes 315 assertions: five exact quiz stdout comparisons, tolerance-equality/hash counterexample, positive-base recurrence solutions, lambda-based RSA decryption, prime-density and password-search arithmetic, crown-graph bad greedy coloring orders, and exhaustive Miller-Rabin bases for odd composites below 200.

Java expressions were checked against Java SE21 Math documentation and integer arithmetic; no Java runtime is installed locally, so they were not executed as Java. No TLS, RSA library, package installer, real compiler allocator or distributed database integration was run.

Cryptographic routines are teaching examples, explicitly not constant-time production primitives. Operation-count, primality-density and assumed password-throughput calculations are models, not measured security/latency guarantees. Existing explicit RSA benchmark/threat-model gap remains.

Historical graph citations checked against IBM publication record, MIT ACM bibliography and four-color theorem coauthor page. Lamé1844 attribution has author-paper search evidence but its full PDF could not be retrieved; no claim of full archival verification. Full MIT2018 textbook exceeded web-tool size; smaller official chapter PDFs were retrieved instead.

Global link-check evidence is inherited from docs/audit-links.json; newly consulted primary pages fetched during this review. Link reachability is distinct from semantic support and is not counted as a factual correction.
